names: Mother of King Bao of Wei
Wife of King Bao of Wei

sourceDate.text: 參為漢相國，出入三年。卒
楚懷王以沛公為碭郡長
參為漢相國出入三年卒

value.cause: defeated and killed by Zhang Han
implicated with Crown Prince and put to death

units.zh: 平陽侯曹參者，沛人也。
units.en: Cao Shen, the Marquis of Pingyang, was a native of Pei.
units.literal: Marquis Pingyang Cao Shen was a native of Pei.

units.zh: 秦時為沛獄掾，而蕭何為主吏，居縣為豪吏矣。
units.en: Under the Qin, he served as the assistant jailer in Pei, while Xiao He was the chief clerk. Both were among the most prominent officials in the county.
units.literal: During Qin times he served as assistant jailer in Pei, while Xiao He was the chief clerk—they were both outstanding officials in the county.

units.zh: 高祖為沛公而初起也，參以中涓從。
units.en: When Gaozu first rose as the Lord of Pei, Cao Shen joined him as a personal attendant.
units.literal: When Gaozu rose as Duke of Pei, Cao Shen followed as an attendant.

units.zh: 將擊胡陵、方與，攻秦監公軍，大破之。
units.en: Leading the attack on Huling and Fangyu, he engaged the army of the Qin Inspector and routed it.
units.literal: He led attacks on Huling and Fangyu, assaulting the Qin Inspector's army and greatly defeating it.

units.zh: 東下薛，擊泗水守軍薛郭西。
units.en: Marching east, he took Xue and struck the Sishui commandery garrison west of the outer walls of Xue.
units.literal: He advanced east to Xue, attacking the garrison of the Si River warden west of Xue's outer walls.

units.zh: 復攻胡陵，取之。
units.en: A second assault captured Huling.
units.literal: He attacked Huling again and captured it.

units.zh: 徙守方與。
units.en: He was then reassigned to defend Fangyu.
units.literal: He was transferred to defend Fangyu.

units.zh: 方與反為魏，擊之。
units.en: When Fangyu defected to Wei, he attacked it.
units.literal: Fangyu defected to Wei, so he attacked it.

units.zh: 豐反為魏，攻之。
units.en: When Feng defected to Wei, he attacked it as well.
units.literal: Feng defected to Wei, so he attacked it.

units.zh: 賜爵七大夫。
units.en: He was awarded the rank of Seventh-Order Grandee.
units.literal: He was granted the rank of Seventh Rank Noble.

units.zh: 擊秦司馬夷軍碭東，破之，取碭、狐父、祁善置。
units.en: Against the army of the Qin Marshal Yi east of Dang, he won a victory and captured Dang, Hufu, and Qishan.
units.literal: He attacked the Qin Marshal Yi's army east of Dang, defeated it, and captured Dang, Hufu, and Qishanzhi.

units.zh: 又攻下邑以西，至虞，擊章邯車騎。
units.en: Advancing west from Xiayi to Yu, he engaged Zhang Han's chariot and cavalry forces.
units.literal: He further attacked west from Xiayi to Yu, attacking Zhang Han's chariots and cavalry.

units.zh: 攻爰戚及亢父，先登。
units.en: At Yuanqi and Kangfu he stormed the walls and was the first man over them.
units.literal: He attacked Yuanqi and Kangfu, being first to scale the walls.

units.zh: 遷為五大夫。
units.en: He was promoted to the rank of Fifth-Order Grandee.
units.literal: He was promoted to Fifth Rank Noble.

units.zh: 北救阿，擊章邯軍，陷陳，追至濮陽。
units.en: Marching north to relieve E, he attacked Zhang Han's army, broke through its battle lines, and pursued the enemy as far as Puyang.
units.literal: He went north to rescue E, attacked Zhang Han's army, broke through their formations, and pursued to Puyang.

units.zh: 攻定陶，取臨濟。
units.en: At Dingtao he attacked and took Linji.
units.literal: He attacked Dingtao and captured Linji.

units.zh: 南救雍丘。
units.en: He went south to relieve the siege of Yongqiu.
units.literal: He went south to rescue Yongqiu.

units.zh: 擊李由軍，破之，殺李由，虜秦候一人。
units.en: In the battle against the army of Li You, he defeated the enemy, slew Li You, and captured a Qin marquis.
units.literal: He attacked Li You's army, defeated it, killed Li You, and captured one Qin noble.

units.zh: 秦將章邯破殺項梁也，沛公與項羽引而東。
units.en: After the Qin general Zhang Han defeated and killed Xiang Liang, the Lord of Pei and Xiang Yu withdrew their forces eastward.
units.literal: When Qin general Zhang Han defeated and killed Xiang Liang, the Duke of Pei and Xiang Yu led their armies east.

units.zh: 楚懷王以沛公為碭郡長，將碭郡兵。
units.en: King Huai of Chu appointed the Lord of Pei as the governor of Dang commandery and placed the commandery's troops under his command.
units.literal: King Huai of Chu appointed the Duke of Pei as governor of Dang commandery to lead Dang commandery troops.

units.zh: 於是乃封參為執帛，號曰建成君。
units.en: Thereupon Cao Shen was given the title of Holder of Silk and styled Lord of Jiancheng.
units.literal: Thus, he enfeoffed Cao Shen as Holder of Silk, with the title Lord Jiancheng.

units.zh: 遷為戚公，屬碭郡。
units.en: He was promoted to the rank of Lord of Qi, under the jurisdiction of Dang commandery.
units.literal: He was promoted to Lord of Qi, belonging to Dang commandery.

units.zh: 其後從攻東郡尉軍，破之成武南。
units.en: Afterward, he joined in attacking the army of the Dongjun commandant and defeated it south of Chengwu.
units.literal: Afterwards he followed in attacking the Dongjun warden's army, defeating it south of Chengwu.

units.zh: 擊王離軍成陽南，復攻之杠裏，大破之。
units.en: Against Wang Li's army south of Chengyang, he pressed the attack again at Gangli and crushed it.
units.literal: He attacked Wang Li's army south of Chengyang, then attacked it again at Gangli, greatly defeating it.

units.zh: 追北，西至開封，擊趙賁軍，破之，圍趙賁開封城中。
units.en: Pursuing the fleeing enemy westward to Kaifeng, he defeated Zhao Ben's army and besieged Zhao Ben within the city walls.
units.literal: He pursued the routed enemy west to Kaifeng, attacked Zhao Ben's army, defeated it, and besieged Zhao Ben in Kaifeng city.

units.zh: 西擊將楊熊軍於曲遇，破之，虜秦司馬及御史各一人。
units.en: Striking west against General Yang Xiong's army at Quyu, he defeated it and captured a Qin marshal and an imperial censor.
units.literal: He attacked General Yang Xiong's army at Quyü to the west, defeated it, and captured one Qin marshal and one imperial secretary each.

units.zh: 遷為執珪。
units.en: He was promoted to the rank of Holder of Jade.
units.literal: He was promoted to Holder of Jade.

units.zh: 從攻陽武，下軒轅、緱氏，絕河津，還擊趙賁軍尸北，破之。
units.en: Joining the attack on Yangwu, he took Xuanyuan and Goushi, severed the river crossings, then wheeled back to defeat Zhao Ben's army north of Shi.
units.literal: He followed in attacking Yangwu, captured Xuanyuan and Goushi, cut off the river crossings, returned to attack Zhao Ben's army north of Shi, and defeated it.

units.zh: 從南攻犨，與南陽守齮戰陽城郭東，陷陳，取宛，虜齮，盡定南陽郡。
units.en: Marching south against Chou, he fought the Nanyang governor Yi east of Yangcheng's walls, broke through the enemy lines, captured Wan, took Yi prisoner, and brought the entire Nanyang commandery under control.
units.literal: He followed south attacking Yan, fought with the Nanyang warden Yi east of Yangcheng's outer walls, broke through formations, captured Wan, captured Yi, and completely pacified Nanyang commandery.

units.zh: 從西攻武關、峣關，取之。
units.en: Pressing westward, he attacked and captured Wuguan and Yaoguan.
units.literal: He followed west attacking Wuguan and Yaoguan, capturing them.

units.zh: 前攻秦軍藍田南，又夜擊其北，秦軍大破，遂至咸陽，滅秦。
units.en: Cao Shen advanced against the Qin army south of Lantian, then struck its northern flank by night. The Qin army was shattered, and the Han forces pressed on to Xianyang, bringing the Qin dynasty to its end.
units.literal: He advanced attacking the Qin army south of Lantian, then at night attacked its north, the Qin army was greatly defeated, thus reaching Xianyang and destroying Qin.

units.zh: 項羽至，以沛公為漢王。
units.en: When Xiang Yu arrived, he installed the Lord of Pei as King of Han.
units.literal: When Xiang Yu arrived, he made the Duke of Pei King of Han.

units.zh: 漢王封參為建成侯。
units.en: The King of Han granted Cao Shen the title Marquis of Jiancheng.
units.literal: The King of Han enfeoffed Cao Shen as Marquis of Jiancheng.

units.zh: 從至漢中，遷為將軍。
units.en: He accompanied the king to Hanzhong and was promoted to general.
units.literal: He followed to Hanzhong, promoted to general.

units.zh: 從還定三秦，初攻下辯、故道、雍、斄。
units.en: In the campaign to return and pacify the Three Qin kingdoms, he first took Xiabian, Gudao, Yong, and Tai.
units.literal: He followed returning to pacify the Three Qins, initially attacking and capturing Bian, Gudao, Yong, and Lai.

units.zh: 擊章平軍於好畤南，破之，圍好畤，取壤鄉。
units.en: At Haozhi, he defeated Zhang Ping's army south of the city, then besieged Haozhi and seized Rangxiang.
units.literal: He attacked Zhang Ping's army south of Haozhi, defeated it, besieged Haozhi, and captured Rangxiang.

units.zh: 擊三秦軍壤東及高櫟，破之。
units.en: Against the Three Qin forces east of Rang and at Gaoli, he won another victory.
units.literal: He attacked the Three Qins army east of Rang and at Gaoque, defeating it.

units.zh: 復圍章平，章平出好畤走。
units.en: Zhang Ping was besieged once more and fled from Haozhi.
units.literal: He besieged Zhang Ping again, Zhang Ping fled from Haozhi.

units.zh: 因擊趙賁、內史保軍，破之。
units.en: Turning next against Zhao Ben and the Grand Administrator Bao, he defeated both armies.
units.literal: He then attacked Zhao Ben and Grand Administrator Bao's army, defeating it.

units.zh: 東取咸陽，更名曰新城。
units.en: Xianyang was taken to the east and renamed Xincheng.
units.literal: He captured Xianyang to the east, renaming it New City.

units.zh: 參將兵守景陵二十日，三秦使章平等攻參，參出擊，大破之。
units.en: Cao Shen garrisoned Jingling for twenty days. When the Three Qin kingdoms dispatched Zhang Ping and others to attack him, he sallied forth and routed them.
units.literal: Cao Shen led troops guarding Jingling for twenty days, the Three Qins sent Zhang Ping and others to attack Cao Shen, Cao Shen sallied to attack, greatly defeating them.

units.zh: 賜食邑於寧秦。
units.en: He was granted a food fief at Ningqin.
units.literal: He was granted fief income in Ningqin.

units.zh: 參以將軍引兵圍章邯於廢丘。
units.en: As general, Cao Shen led his troops to besiege Zhang Han at Feiqiu.
units.literal: Cao Shen as general led troops besieging Zhang Han at Fei Qiu.

units.zh: 以中尉從漢王出臨晉關。
units.en: Serving as Commandant, he accompanied the King of Han through Linjin Pass.
units.literal: As Commandant he followed the King of Han out of Linjin Pass.

units.zh: 至河內，下修武，渡圍津，東擊龍且、項他定陶，破之。
units.en: After reaching Henei, he took Xiuwu, crossed at Weijin, and struck eastward against Long Ju and Xiang Ta at Dingtao, defeating them.
units.literal: Arriving in Henei, he captured Xiuwu, crossed at Weijin, attacked Long Ju and Xiang Ta at Dingtao to the east, defeating them.

units.zh: 東取碭、蕭、彭城。
units.en: From there he marched east to capture Dang, Xiao, and Pengcheng.
units.literal: He captured Dang, Xiao, and Pengcheng to the east.

units.zh: 擊項籍軍，漢軍大敗走。
units.en: In battle with Xiang Yu's army, the Han forces suffered a crushing defeat and fled.
units.literal: He attacked Xiang Yu's army, the Han army suffered great defeat and fled.

units.zh: 參以中尉圍取雍丘。
units.en: As Commandant, Cao Shen besieged and took Yongqiu.
units.literal: Cao Shen as Commandant besieged and captured Yongqiu.

units.zh: 王武反於［外］黃，程處反於燕，往擊，盡破之。
units.en: When Wang Wu revolted at Waihuang and Cheng Chu revolted at Yan, he marched against them and defeated them all.
units.literal: Wang Wu rebelled at Waihuang, Cheng Chu rebelled at Yan, he went to attack them, completely defeating both.

units.zh: 柱天侯反於衍氏，又進破取衍氏。
units.en: The Marquis of Zhutian revolted at Yanshi, and Cao Shen advanced to take the city.
units.literal: Marquis Zhutian rebelled at Yanshi, he advanced and defeated and captured Yanshi.

units.zh: 擊羽嬰於昆陽，追至葉。
units.en: At Kunyang he attacked Yu Ying and pursued him as far as Ye.
units.literal: He attacked Yu Ying at Kunyang, pursuing to Ye.

units.zh: 還攻武彊，因至滎陽。
units.en: Turning back, he attacked Wuqiang and then made his way to Xingyang.
units.literal: He returned attacking Wujiang, thus reaching Xingyang.

units.zh: 參自漢中為將軍中尉，從擊諸侯，及項羽敗，還至滎陽，凡二歲。
units.en: From the time Cao Shen left Hanzhong as General-Commandant, following the campaigns against the feudal lords until Xiang Yu's defeat and the return to Xingyang, two full years had passed.
units.literal: Cao Shen from Hanzhong served as General Commandant, following to attack the feudal lords, and when Xiang Yu was defeated, returned to Xingyang, altogether two years.

units.zh: 高祖（三）［二］年，拜為假左丞相，入屯兵關中。
units.en: In the second year of Gaozu's reign, he was appointed Acting Left Chancellor and entered Guanzhong to garrison the region.
units.literal: In Gaozu year 2, he was appointed Acting Left Chancellor, entering to station troops in Guanzhong.

units.zh: 月餘，魏王豹反，以假左丞相別與韓信東攻魏將軍孫遬軍東張，大破之。
units.en: A little over a month later, King Bao of Wei rebelled. As Acting Left Chancellor, Cao Shen joined Han Xin on a separate campaign eastward, attacking the Wei general Sun Su's army at Dongzhang and routing it.
units.literal: After more than a month, King Wei Bao rebelled, so as Acting Left Chancellor he separately went east with Han Xin to attack Wei general Sun Ju's army at Dongzhang, greatly defeating it.

units.zh: 因攻安邑，得魏將王襄。
units.en: Anyi was then attacked, and the Wei general Wang Xiang was captured.
units.literal: He then attacked Anyi, capturing Wei general Wang Xiang.

units.zh: 擊魏王於曲陽，追至武垣，生得魏王豹。
units.en: At Quyang he struck the King of Wei, pursued him to Wuyuan, and took King Bao of Wei alive.
units.literal: He attacked the King of Wei at Quyang, pursuing to Wuyuan, capturing the King of Wei Bao alive.

units.zh: 取平陽，得魏王母妻子，盡定魏地，凡五十二城。
units.en: Pingyang fell next; he seized the King of Wei's mother, wife, and children, bringing all of Wei's territory under control—fifty-two cities in all.
units.literal: He captured Pingyang, obtaining the King of Wei's mother, wife, and children, completely pacifying Wei territory, altogether fifty-two cities.

units.zh: 賜食邑平陽。
units.en: A food fief at Pingyang was granted to him.
units.literal: He was granted fief income in Pingyang.

units.zh: 因從韓信擊趙相國夏說軍於鄔東，大破之，斬夏說。
units.en: He next joined Han Xin in attacking the Zhao Chancellor Xia Yue's army east of Wu, inflicting a devastating defeat and beheading Xia Yue.
units.literal: He then followed Han Xin attacking Chancellor of Zhao Xia Yue's army east of Wu, greatly defeating it, beheading Xia Yue.

units.zh: 韓信與故常山王張耳引兵下井陘，擊成安君，而令參還圍趙別將戚將軍於鄔城中。
units.en: Han Xin and the former King of Changshan, Zhang Er, led their forces down through the Jingxing Pass to attack the Lord of Cheng'an, while ordering Cao Shen to turn back and besiege the Zhao commander General Qi inside the walls of Wu.
units.literal: Han Xin and former King Changshan Zhang Er led troops down Jingxing, attacking Lord Cheng'an, while ordering Cao Shen to return and besiege Zhao's separate general Lord Qi in Wu city.

units.zh: 戚將軍出走，追斬之。
units.en: General Qi broke out and fled, but Cao Shen pursued and killed him.
units.literal: Lord Qi fled, he pursued and beheaded him.

units.zh: 乃引兵詣敖倉漢王之所。
units.en: From there he led his forces to the Ao Granary, where the King of Han was stationed.
units.literal: He then led troops to Aocang where the King of Han was located.

units.zh: 韓信已破趙，為相國，東擊齊。
units.en: Han Xin, having already conquered Zhao and been made Chancellor, now turned east to attack Qi.
units.literal: Han Xin had already defeated Zhao, became Chancellor, attacking Qi to the east.

units.zh: 參以右丞相屬韓信，攻破齊歷下軍，遂取臨菑。
units.en: As Right Chancellor serving under Han Xin, Cao Shen smashed the Qi army at Lixia and went on to capture the capital Linzi.
units.literal: Cao Shen as Right Chancellor under Han Xin attacked and broke the Qi army at Lixia, thus capturing Linzi.

units.zh: 還定濟北郡，攻著、漯陰、平原、鬲、盧。
units.en: Returning to pacify Jibei commandery, he attacked Zhu, Taoyin, Pingyuan, Ge, and Lu.
units.literal: He returned to pacify Jibei commandery, attacking Zhu, Taoyin, Pingyuan, Ge, and Lu.

units.zh: 已而從韓信擊龍且軍於上假密，大破之，斬龍且，虜其將軍周蘭。
units.en: Soon afterward he joined Han Xin in attacking Long Ju's army at Shangjia. They dealt it a crushing blow, beheading Long Ju and capturing his general Zhou Lan.
units.literal: Soon after he followed Han Xin attacking Long Ju's army at Shang Jiami, greatly defeating it, beheading Long Ju, capturing his general Zhou Lan.

units.zh: 定齊，凡得七十餘縣。
units.en: With Qi fully pacified, they had secured more than seventy counties in all.
units.literal: He pacified Qi, altogether obtaining over seventy counties.

units.zh: 得故齊王田廣相田光，其守相許章，及故齊膠東將軍田既。
units.en: He captured Tian Guang, the chancellor of the former King of Qi Tian Guang; Xu Zhang, the defending chancellor; and Tian Ji, the former Jiaodong general of Qi.
units.literal: He obtained the former King of Qi Tian Guang's chancellor Tian Guang, his defending chancellor Xu Zhang, and the former Jiaodong general of Qi Tian Ji.

units.zh: 韓信為齊王，引兵詣陳，與漢王共破項羽，而參留平齊未服者。
units.en: When Han Xin, now King of Qi, led his forces to Chen to join the King of Han in destroying Xiang Yu, Cao Shen stayed behind to subdue the parts of Qi that had not yet submitted.
units.literal: Han Xin became King of Qi, led troops to Chen, together with the King of Han defeated Xiang Yu, while Cao Shen remained to pacify those in Qi who had not submitted.

units.zh: 項籍已死，天下定，漢王為皇帝，韓信徙為楚王，齊為郡。
units.en: After Xiang Yu's death and the pacification of the realm, the King of Han became emperor. Han Xin was transferred to the kingship of Chu, and Qi was made a commandery.
units.literal: After Xiang Ji died and the realm was pacified, the King of Han became emperor, Han Xin was moved to King of Chu, Qi became a commandery.

units.zh: 參歸漢相印。
units.en: Cao Shen returned the Han chancellor's seal.
units.literal: Cao Shen returned the Han chancellorship seal.

units.zh: 高帝以長子肥為齊王，而以參為齊相國。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu made his eldest son Fei the King of Qi and appointed Cao Shen as the Chancellor of Qi.
units.literal: Gaozu made his eldest son Fei King of Qi, and appointed Cao Shen as Qi's prime minister.

units.zh: 以高祖六年賜爵列侯，與諸侯剖符，世世勿絕。
units.en: In the sixth year of Gaozu's reign, he was granted the rank of full marquis, receiving a tallied covenant with the feudal lords that his line would never be extinguished.
units.literal: In Gaozu year 6 he was granted marquis rank, sharing the tally with feudal lords, never to be extinguished generation after generation.

units.zh: 食邑平陽萬六百三十戶，號曰平陽侯，除前所食邑。
units.en: His fief was set at Pingyang with ten thousand six hundred and thirty households, and he was styled Marquis of Pingyang, superseding all previous fiefs.
units.literal: His fief income was Pingyang with 10,630 households, titled Marquis of Pingyang, removing his previous fief income.

units.zh: 以齊相國擊陳豨將張春軍，破之。
units.en: As Chancellor of Qi, he attacked the army of Chen Xi's general Zhang Chun and defeated it.
units.literal: As Qi prime minister he attacked Chen Xi's general Zhang Chun's army, defeating it.

units.zh: 黥布反，參以齊相國從悼惠王將兵車騎十二萬人，與高祖會擊黥布軍，大破之。
units.en: When Ying Bu revolted, Cao Shen, as Chancellor of Qi, accompanied King Daohui with a force of one hundred and twenty thousand infantry, chariots, and cavalry to join Emperor Gaozu in striking Ying Bu's army. They inflicted a crushing defeat.
units.literal: Ying Bu rebelled, Cao Shen as Qi prime minister followed King Daohui leading troops and chariots of 120,000 men, meeting with Gaozu to attack Ying Bu's army, greatly defeating it.

units.zh: 南至蘄，還定竹邑、相、蕭、留。
units.en: Pressing south as far as Qi, he then turned back to pacify Zhuyi, Xiang, Xiao, and Liu.
units.literal: He went south to Qi, returning to pacify Zhuyi, Xiang, Xiao, and Liu.

units.zh: 參功：凡下二國，縣一百二十二；
units.en: The tally of Cao Shen's achievements was as follows: he conquered two kingdoms and one hundred and twenty-two counties;
units.literal: Cao Shen's merits: Altogether conquered two states, 122 counties;

units.zh: 得王二人，相三人，將軍六人，大莫敖、郡守、司馬、候、御史各一人。
units.en: he captured two kings, three chancellors, six generals, one Grand Moao, one commandery governor, one marshal, one marquis, and one imperial secretary.
units.literal: captured two kings, three chancellors, six generals, one Grand Moao, one commandery governor, one marshal, one noble, one imperial secretary each.

units.zh: 孝惠帝元年，除諸侯相國法，更以參為齊丞相。
units.en: In the first year of Emperor Hui's reign, the law governing the appointment of feudal chancellors was abolished, and Cao Shen's title was changed to Chancellor of Qi.
units.literal: In Emperor Hui year 1, the law for feudal lords' prime ministers was abolished, changing Cao Shen to Qi chancellor.

units.zh: 參之相齊，齊七十城。
units.en: When Cao Shen served as Chancellor of Qi, the kingdom comprised seventy cities.
units.literal: When Cao Shen served as chancellor of Qi, Qi had seventy cities.

units.zh: 天下初定，悼惠王富於春秋，參盡召長老諸生，問所以安集百姓，如齊故［俗］諸儒以百數，言人人殊，參未知所定。
units.en: The realm had only just been settled, and King Daohui was still young. Cao Shen summoned all the elders and scholars to ask how best to bring peace and stability to the people. The Confucian scholars of Qi numbered in the hundreds, and each one had a different answer, so Cao Shen could not decide on a course of action.
units.literal: The realm had just been pacified, King Daohui was young, Cao Shen summoned all the elders and scholars, asking how to pacify and gather the people, scholars of Qi custom numbered in the hundreds, each speaking differently, Cao Shen did not know what to decide.

units.zh: 聞膠西有蓋公，善治黃老言，使人厚幣請之。
units.en: He then heard that in Jiaoxi there lived a certain Master Gai, well versed in the teachings of Huang-Lao, and sent emissaries bearing generous gifts to invite him.
units.literal: He heard there was Master Gai in Jiaoxi who was skilled in Huang-Lao teachings, sent people with generous gifts to invite him.

units.zh: 既見蓋公，蓋公為言治道貴清靜而民自定，推此類具言之。
units.en: When they met, Master Gai explained that the essence of good governance lies in prizing stillness and non-interference, so that the people settle of their own accord. He elaborated on this principle at length.
units.literal: When he met Master Gai, Master Gai spoke of the way of governance valuing tranquility and the people naturally settling, elaborating on this category comprehensively.

units.zh: 參於是避正堂，舍蓋公焉。
units.en: Cao Shen thereupon vacated his own principal hall and lodged Master Gai in it.
units.literal: Thus, Cao Shen vacated the main hall and housed Master Gai there.

units.zh: 其治要用黃老術，故相齊九年，齊國安集，大稱賢相。
units.en: The core of his administration rested on Huang-Lao methods. He served as Chancellor of Qi for nine years, during which the kingdom was peaceful and orderly, and he was universally acclaimed as a worthy chancellor.
units.literal: His governance essentials used Huang-Lao methods, thus serving as chancellor of Qi for nine years, Qi was pacified and stable, greatly acclaimed as a worthy chancellor.

units.zh: 惠帝二年，蕭何卒。
units.en: In the second year of Emperor Hui's reign, Xiao He died.
units.literal: In Emperor Hui year 2, Xiao He died.

units.zh: 參聞之，告舍人趣治行，「吾將入相」。
units.en: When Cao Shen heard the news, he told his retainers to pack at once, saying, "I am about to be summoned to serve as chancellor."
units.literal: Cao Shen heard of it, told his retainers to quickly prepare for travel, 'I will enter as prime minister.'

units.zh: 居無何，使者果召參。
units.en: Before long, imperial envoys arrived to summon him, just as he had predicted.
units.literal: Before long, envoys indeed summoned Cao Shen.

units.zh: 參去，屬其後相曰：「以齊獄市為寄，慎勿擾也。」
units.en: Before departing, Cao Shen instructed his successor as chancellor: "Treat the prisons and markets of Qi as a sacred trust, and take care not to meddle with them."
units.literal: Cao Shen departed, instructing his successor chancellor: 'Consider Qi's prisons and markets as entrusted, do not disturb them.'

units.zh: 後相曰：「治無大於此者乎？」
units.en: The new chancellor asked, "Is there truly nothing more important in governing than this?"
units.literal: The successor chancellor said: 'Is there nothing more important than this in governance?'

units.zh: 參曰：「不然。
units.en: Cao Shen replied, "No, that is not so.
units.literal: Cao Shen said: 'Not so.

units.zh: 夫獄市者，所以并容也，今君擾之，姦人安所容也？
units.en: The prisons and markets are places that accommodate all sorts of people. If you interfere with them, where will the troublemakers go?
units.literal: Prisons and markets are for accommodating all sorts—now if you disturb them, where will wicked people find accommodation?

units.zh: 吾是以先之。」
units.en: That is why I place this matter above all else."
units.literal: This is why I put it first.'

units.zh: 參始微時，與蕭何善；
units.en: In his early, humble days, Cao Shen had been close friends with Xiao He;
units.literal: Cao Shen from humble beginnings was on good terms with Xiao He;

units.zh: 及為將相，有卻。
units.en: but once they rose to become generals and chancellors, a rift grew between them.
units.literal: when they became generals and chancellors, there was some distance.

units.zh: 至何且死，所推賢唯參。
units.en: Yet when Xiao He lay on his deathbed, the only man he recommended as worthy to succeed him was Cao Shen.
units.literal: When Xiao He was about to die, the worthy he recommended was only Cao Shen.

units.zh: 參代何為漢相國，舉事無所變更，一遵蕭何約束。
units.en: Cao Shen succeeded Xiao He as Chancellor of Han. In all matters of governance he changed nothing, adhering strictly to the regulations Xiao He had established.
units.literal: Cao Shen succeeded Xiao He as Han prime minister, in handling affairs he changed nothing, strictly following Xiao He's regulations.

units.zh: 擇郡國吏木詘於文辭，重厚長者，即召除為丞相史。
units.en: He selected for his staff officials from the commanderies and kingdoms who were plain-spoken and clumsy with fine phrases—solid, steady men of mature character—and summoned them to serve as secretaries of the chancellor.
units.literal: He selected commandery and state officials who were clumsy with literary phrases, solid and mature elders, immediately summoning and appointing them as chancellor secretaries.

units.zh: 吏之言文刻深，欲務聲名者，輒斥去之。
units.en: Any official who spoke with legalistic precision and severity, or who was eager to make a name for himself, he immediately dismissed.
units.literal: Officials who spoke of literary precision and harshness, desiring to pursue reputation, he immediately dismissed them.

units.zh: 日夜飲醇酒。
units.en: Day and night he drank mellow wine.
units.literal: Day and night he drank strong wine.

units.zh: 卿大夫已下吏及賓客見參不事事，來者皆欲有言。
units.en: The ministers, grandees, lower officials, and guests who observed Cao Shen doing nothing at all were eager to admonish him.
units.literal: Ministers, grandees, and lower officials as well as guests saw Cao Shen doing nothing, visitors all wished to speak.

units.zh: 至者，參輒飲以醇酒，閒之，欲有所言，復飲之，醉而後去，終莫得開說，以為常。
units.en: Whenever anyone came to call, Cao Shen would immediately ply them with strong wine. When they tried to broach the subject of government, he poured them yet more wine until they departed drunk, never having had a chance to speak their minds. This became his settled practice.
units.literal: Those who arrived, Cao Shen always plied them with strong wine; if they wished to speak, he gave them more to drink—they left drunk, never able to get a word in, and this became the norm.

units.zh: 相舍後園近吏舍，吏舍日飲歌呼。
units.en: The rear garden of the chancellor's residence adjoined the clerks' quarters, and the clerks drank and sang boisterously every day.
units.literal: The prime minister's residence back garden was near the official quarters, the official quarters daily drank and sang loudly.

units.zh: 從吏惡之，無如之何，乃請參游園中，聞吏醉歌呼，從吏幸相國召按之。
units.en: His attendants found this unbearable but could do nothing about it. They invited Cao Shen to stroll through the garden, hoping that when he heard the drunken singing of the clerks, the chancellor would call them in for a reprimand.
units.literal: The attendants hated it, but could do nothing about it, so they requested Cao Shen to stroll in the garden, hearing the officials drunk singing loudly, hoping the prime minister would summon and investigate them.

units.zh: 乃反取酒張坐飲，亦歌呼與相應和。
units.en: Instead, Cao Shen sent for wine, spread mats, and sat down to drink, joining in the singing and calling back and forth with the clerks.
units.literal: Instead he brought wine and spread mats to sit and drink, also singing loudly in response and harmony.

units.zh: 參見人之有細過，專掩匿覆蓋之，府中無事。
units.en: Whenever Cao Shen noticed someone committing a minor offense, he made a point of covering it up and overlooking it, and the chancellery remained free of trouble.
units.literal: When Cao Shen saw people with minor faults, he specially concealed and covered them up, and the chancellery was without incident.

units.zh: 參子窋為中大夫。
units.en: Cao Shen's son Zhu served as a Palace Grandee.
units.literal: Cao Shen's son Zhu served as Palace Grandee.

units.zh: 惠帝怪相國不治事，以為「豈少朕與」？
units.en: Emperor Hui found it strange that the chancellor took no interest in governance, and wondered, "Could it be that he thinks little of me?"
units.literal: Emperor Hui was surprised the prime minister did not handle affairs, thinking, "Could it be that he thinks little of me?"

units.zh: 乃謂窋曰：「若歸，試私從容問而父曰：『高帝新棄群臣，帝富於春秋，君為相，日飲，無所請事，何以憂天下乎？』
units.en: So the emperor told Zhu, "When you go home, find a quiet moment and ask your father casually: 'Emperor Gaozu has only recently departed from his ministers. The emperor is young, and you, the chancellor, do nothing but drink all day. You never bring a single matter before the throne. How can you claim to be worrying about the realm?'
units.literal: He then told Zhu, "When you return, try privately and at your leisure to ask your father, 'Gaozu has newly abandoned his ministers; the emperor is still young; you serve as chancellor, yet you drink all day and bring no business before the throne—how can you claim to be worrying about the realm?'

units.zh: 然無言吾告若也。」
units.en: But do not let on that I put you up to it."
units.literal: However, do not say I told you."

units.zh: 窋既洗沐歸，窋侍，自從其所諫參。
units.en: On his next rest day, Zhu went home. While attending his father, he followed the emperor's instructions and raised the matter with Cao Shen.
units.literal: Zhu, having bathed and returned, while attending his father, privately followed the emperor's instructions and remonstrated with Cao Shen.

units.zh: 參怒，而笞窋二百，曰：「趣入侍，天下事非若所當言也。」
units.en: Cao Shen flew into a rage and had Zhu caned two hundred strokes, saying, "Get back to the palace and attend the emperor. The affairs of the realm are no concern of yours."
units.literal: Cao Shen was angry and caned Zhu two hundred strokes, saying, "Hurry back to attend the emperor—the affairs of the realm are not for you to speak of."

units.zh: 至朝時，惠帝讓參曰：「與窋胡治乎？
units.en: At the next audience, Emperor Hui reproached Cao Shen: "Why did you punish Zhu?
units.literal: At court, Emperor Hui reproached Cao Shen, saying, "Why did you punish Zhu?

units.zh: 乃者我使諫君也。」
units.en: It was I who told him to speak with you."
units.literal: It was I who sent him to remonstrate with you.'

units.zh: 參免冠謝曰：「陛下自察聖武孰與高帝？」
units.en: Cao Shen doffed his cap and apologized, then asked, "Would Your Majesty say that in sagely martial virtue you are the equal of Emperor Gaozu?"
units.literal: Cao Shen removed his cap and apologized: 'Your majesty yourself examine—whose sagely martial qualities compare with Gaozu's?'

units.zh: 上曰：「朕乃安敢望先帝乎！」
units.en: The emperor replied, "How would I dare compare myself to the former emperor!"
units.literal: The emperor said: 'How would I dare aspire to the former emperor!'

units.zh: 曰：「陛下觀臣能孰與蕭何賢？」
units.en: Cao Shen continued, "And does Your Majesty consider me the equal of Xiao He in ability?"
units.literal: Cao Shen said, "Your Majesty, whose ability do you consider the equal of Xiao He's?"

units.zh: 上曰：「君似不及也。」
units.en: The emperor said, "You do not seem to be his equal."
units.literal: The emperor said: 'You seem not to match him.'

units.zh: 參曰：「陛下言之是也。
units.en: Cao Shen said, "Your Majesty speaks truly.
units.literal: Cao Shen said: 'Your majesty's words are correct.

units.zh: 且高帝與蕭何定天下，法令既明，今陛下垂拱，參等守職，遵而勿失，不亦可乎？」
units.en: Emperor Gaozu and Xiao He pacified the realm, and the laws and ordinances they laid down are clear. Now if Your Majesty sits with folded hands, and men like myself faithfully guard our posts, following those precedents without deviation—is that not sufficient?"
units.literal: Moreover, Gaozu and Xiao He pacified the realm, laws and ordinances already clear, now your majesty hangs sleeves and does nothing, we and others guard our positions, follow without losing them—is this not acceptable?'

units.zh: 惠帝曰：「善。
units.en: Emperor Hui said, "Very well.
units.literal: Emperor Hui said: 'Good.

units.zh: 君休矣！」
units.en: You may retire."
units.literal: You are excused!'

units.zh: 參為漢相國，出入三年。
units.en: Cao Shen served as Chancellor of Han for a little over three years.
units.literal: Cao Shen served as Han prime minister for three years coming and going.

units.zh: 卒，謚懿侯。
units.en: When he died, he was given the posthumous title Marquis Yi.
units.literal: He died, given the posthumous title Marquis Yi.

units.zh: 子窋代侯。
units.en: His son Zhu succeeded to the marquisate.
units.literal: His son Zhu succeeded as marquis.

units.zh: 百姓歌之曰：「蕭何為法，顜若畫一；
units.en: The common people sang of him: "Xiao He framed the laws, clear-cut as lines drawn with a ruler;
units.literal: The people sang of him: 'Xiao He made the laws, precise as if drawn by rule;

units.zh: 曹參代之，守而勿失。
units.en: Cao Shen took his place and kept them without fail.
units.literal: Cao Shen succeeded him, guarded without losing.

units.zh: 載其清凈，民以寧一。」
units.en: He upheld their purity and stillness, and the people found peace and unity."
units.literal: Carried his clarity and purity, the people achieved peace and unity.'

units.zh: 平陽侯窋，高后時為御史大夫。
units.en: The Marquis of Pingyang, Zhu, served as Grand Censor during the time of Empress Dowager Gao.
units.literal: The Marquis of Pingyang, Zhu, during Empress Gao's time served as Grand Censor.

units.zh: 孝文帝立，免為侯。
units.en: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Zhu was relieved of his post and reverted to his status as marquis.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen was established, he was dismissed to become marquis.

units.zh: 立二十九年卒，謚為靜侯。
units.en: He held the marquisate for twenty-nine years before he died, and was given the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
units.literal: He reigned twenty-nine years and died, given the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

units.zh: 子奇代侯，立七年卒，謚為簡侯。
units.en: His son Qi succeeded to the marquisate, held it for seven years, and died. He was given the posthumous title Marquis Jian.
units.literal: His son Qi succeeded as marquis, reigned seven years and died, given the posthumous title Marquis Jian.

units.zh: 子時代侯。
units.en: His son Shi succeeded to the marquisate.
units.literal: His son Shi succeeded as marquis.

units.zh: 時尚平陽公主，生子襄。
units.en: Shi married the Princess of Pingyang and fathered a son named Xiang.
units.literal: Shi married Princess Pingyang, fathering son Xiang.

units.zh: 時病癘，歸國。
units.en: Shi contracted a severe illness and returned to his domain.
units.literal: Shi fell ill and returned to his state.

units.zh: 立二十三年卒，謚夷侯。
units.en: He held the marquisate for twenty-three years before he died, and was given the posthumous title Marquis Yi.
units.literal: He reigned twenty-three years and died, given the posthumous title Marquis Yi.

units.zh: 子襄代侯。
units.en: His son Xiang succeeded to the marquisate.
units.literal: His son Xiang succeeded as marquis.

units.zh: 襄尚衛長公主，生子宗。
units.en: Xiang married the Elder Princess of Wei and fathered a son named Zong.
units.literal: Xiang married the Elder Princess of Wei, fathering son Zong.

units.zh: 立十六年卒，謚為共侯。
units.en: He held the marquisate for sixteen years before he died, and was given the posthumous title Marquis Gong.
units.literal: He reigned sixteen years and died, given the posthumous title Marquis Gong.

units.zh: 子宗代侯。
units.en: His son Zong succeeded to the marquisate.
units.literal: His son Zong succeeded as marquis.

units.zh: 征和二年中，宗坐太子死，國除。
units.en: In the second year of the Zhenghe era, Zong was implicated in the affair of the Crown Prince and put to death, and the marquisate was abolished.
units.literal: In Zhenghe year 2, Zong was implicated in the crown prince's death, the state abolished.

units.zh: 太史公曰：曹相國參攻城野戰之功所以能多若此者，以與淮陰侯俱。
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: The reason Chancellor Cao Shen was able to amass so many achievements in besieging cities and fighting in the field was that he served alongside the Marquis of Huaiyin.
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: Chancellor Cao Shen's merits in attacking cities and field battles could be so many because he was together with the Marquis of Huaiyin.

units.zh: 及信已滅，而列侯成功，唯獨參擅其名。
units.en: After Han Xin was destroyed and the marquises' accomplishments were tallied, it was Cao Shen alone who claimed the foremost reputation.
units.literal: When Xin was already extinguished, while the marquises achieved success, only Cao Shen monopolized the name.

units.zh: 參為漢相國，清靜極言合道。
units.en: As Chancellor of Han, Cao Shen governed through stillness and non-interference, in perfect accord with the Way.
units.literal: Cao Shen as Han prime minister, his clarity and tranquility reached the extreme of accord with the Way.

units.zh: 然百姓離秦之酷後，參與休息無為，故天下俱稱其美矣。
units.en: The people had only just escaped Qin's cruelty, and Cao Shen let them recover through quiet, noninterference; for this, the whole realm praised his virtue.
units.literal: The people had only just emerged from the cruelties of Qin, and Cao Shen gave them rest through inaction—a wordplay on his name—and for this the entire realm praised his virtue.
